_note: Substances/routes where a data source's DOSE ladder is skipped at ingest, so the next-priority source backfills. A declarative override (with a reason) instead of duplicating corrected dose data in the curated layer. Omit `routes` to skip that source's doses for the whole substance. An entry that suppresses nothing on a route it names fails the build. Every entry carries either a `citation` - a PMID, DOI, ISBN or label set_id for the fact its `note` rests on - or a `reason_only` sentence saying why no source can be cited, and the reason_only entries are a shrink-only list in pipeline/build/tests/reason-only-baseline.json. PIHKAL/TIHKAL no-activity bounds need no entry: the build reads the book's DOSAGE clause and refuses them (pipeline/build/dose_gates.py). Each should also be reported upstream for a real fix.

drug.community.name: Amobarbital
drug.community.note: dc IV common > oral. For a barbiturate that inverts the route: an intravenous dose reaches the circulation whole, so it cannot need more drug than the same source's own oral ladder.
drug.community.reason_only: No label or clinical source for parenteral amobarbital is indexed (openFDA, DailyMed and Drugs@FDA all return nothing; PubMed has only the intracarotid Wada test, a different indication). The defect is internal to the source.

drug.community.name: Atropine
drug.community.note: common 2-5 / strong 6-10 mg. The labeled adult systemic dose is 0.5-1 mg with a 3 mg maximum total, so this ladder's common tier starts above a full labeled dose, and a documented 15 mg oral exposure produced an acute anticholinergic syndrome needing mechanical ventilation. Only source for the oral route; the IV antidote ladder is correct and stays.
citation: DailyMed Atropine Sulfate Injection (Fresenius Kabi, NDA209260), set_id 310c8a74-ea24-4357-8099-81e394b1634e, §2.2

drug.community.name: Bromoketamine
drug.community.note: threshold 0.3 / common 0.7-1 mg against this same source's own insufflation ladder of 90-160 mg — a 100x internal contradiction, almost certainly mg/kg recorded as absolute mg. The substance is tagged no-human-data.
drug.community.reason_only: Nothing external to cite: the contradiction is inside the source's own rows, and no study of this compound in humans exists to put a number against them.

drug.community.name: Cocaine
drug.community.note: dc's IV ladder is its own insufflation ladder verbatim, which inverts the route: intranasal cocaine is about 80% bioavailable (Jeffcoat 1989, pmid:2565204), so an intravenous dose cannot need as much drug — and shipping it also puts IV above this source's smoked ladder. The size of the error is smaller than it looks: human laboratory studies give 20 mg as a fixed IV dose (pmid:23144826) and 0.23-0.46 mg/kg per injection (pmid:30811963), so the wiki ladder that backfills here (common 5-10 mg) sits BELOW the supervised range while dc's sits above it. No source gives a defensible IV ladder, so the bad shape is dropped and no number is invented in its place; the understatement that remains is recorded here rather than silently fixed.

drug.community.name: Mitragynine
drug.community.note: A kratom-LEAF ladder on the pure alkaloid: the row is in grams and its own unit string says "g (leaf powder)", while its note gives the leaf's alkaloid content as 12-21 mg/g — so the numbers describe plant material roughly a thousandfold weaker than the compound the row is filed under. Piru's own mitragynine ladder is in mg and the leaf ladders live on the Kratom row. Not yet reported upstream.
drug.community.reason_only: Nothing external to cite: the row identifies itself as leaf material in its own unit string and note, so the mismatch with the compound it is filed under needs no outside source.

drug.community.name: MXP
drug.community.note: drug.community files this as "MXP (Methoxphenidine)", so the exception keys on the split short name. MXP is documented oral and insufflated only — not formulated or characterized for injection. The routes the literature describes are oral, sublingual and intranasal (Jurásek 2022, pmid:35216198). Offering an IV ladder is an invitation, not a reference.

drug.community.name: Para-Methoxyamphetamine
drug.community.note: PMA under its full name. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.
drug.community.citation: EMCDDA, Report on the risk assessment of PMMA in the framework of the joint action on new synthetic drugs, Risk Assessments No. 5 (2003), ISBN 92-9168-137-7

drug.community.name: Quetiapine
drug.community.note: dc's ladder is the antipsychotic's THERAPEUTIC regime, not a ladder: its tiers reproduce the labeled recommended ranges (150-750 mg/day for schizophrenia, 400-800 mg/day for bipolar mania). The claim is not that the figures are too high — they are the label's own — but that a prescription antipsychotic's treatment dose must not ship as a dose ladder; the sedative-dose ladder the other four sources carry is what ships. If assign_dose_contexts ever tags this row therapeutic, strip_medical_rx_doses owns it and this entry goes.

psychonautwiki.name: Citicoline
psychonautwiki.note: PsychonautWiki's name for CDP-Choline; it ingests under this name and is merged into CDP-Choline afterwards. total 58-74 h, offset 30-40 h, afterglow 40-60 h against a measured human exposure of hours: plasma choline stays significantly elevated for 5, 8 and 10 h after 500, 2000 and 4000 mg oral doses (Wurtman 2000, pmid:10974208), and plasma levels peak at 1 h (pmid:26366063). piru-curated (8-24 h) already outranks the total, but per-phase resolution meant the bad offset and afterglow still resolved from here — masking is not fixing.

psychonautwiki.name: Midazolam
psychonautwiki.note: peak 1-4 h on the drug chosen for procedural sedation precisely because it peaks in minutes (t1/2 1.5-2.5 h). drug.community's 15 min backfills. Intranasal and IV midazolam sedation in 12 volunteers set in within 5–10 and 3–4 min and lasted about 40 and 35 min (Gudmundsdottir 2001, pmid:11802661).

psychonautwiki.name: Naloxone
psychonautwiki.note: Oral bioavailability is under 2% and the label states that oral naloxone has no pharmacologic activity at a dose that antagonises pentazocine when given parenterally; naloxone is in Suboxone precisely because it is systemically inactive by mouth. A 5-15 min onset and 1-2 h total for oral dosing is pharmacokinetically impossible, and offering the route at all implies an opioid reversal that will not happen.
citation: DailyMed Pentazocine and Naloxone Tablets, set_id a28450a0-ac93-4235-b9a6-58cdf24773cb, §Clinical Pharmacology

psychonautwiki.name: Nifoxipam
psychonautwiki.note: total 10-75 h. No measured human half-life or duration for nifoxipam exists: the 15 indexed papers are analytical-method, metabolite-identification and poison-centre work, and the only duration figures in the literature come from internet trip reports (pmid:31971477). A 75 h upper bound rests on nothing, so it is not shipped. TripSit's 10-18 h backfills.

psychonautwiki.name: PMA
psychonautwiki.note: threshold 10 / light 20-40 / common 40-60 mg and NO strong or heavy tier, which reads as "nothing above this is defined" rather than "above this kills". PMA/PMMA blood levels >0.5 mg/L are toxic-to-lethal against a fatal median of 1.92 mg/L. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.
psychonautwiki.citation: EMCDDA, Report on the risk assessment of PMMA in the framework of the joint action on new synthetic drugs, Risk Assessments No. 5 (2003), ISBN 92-9168-137-7

psychonautwiki.name: PMMA
psychonautwiki.note: a single 100-120 mg "common" tier already inside the reported lethal range; recreational and lethal exposure overlap with no separable window. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.
psychonautwiki.citation: EMCDDA, Report on the risk assessment of PMMA in the framework of the joint action on new synthetic drugs, Risk Assessments No. 5 (2003), ISBN 92-9168-137-7

freeodwiki.name: Naloxone
freeodwiki.note: See the psychonautwiki entry — oral naloxone is ~2% bioavailable and systemically inactive.

freeodwiki.name: Para-Methoxyamphetamine
freeodwiki.note: PMA under its full name. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.
freeodwiki.citation: EMCDDA, Report on the risk assessment of PMMA in the framework of the joint action on new synthetic drugs, Risk Assessments No. 5 (2003), ISBN 92-9168-137-7

freeodwiki.name: PMMA
freeodwiki.note: Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.
freeodwiki.citation: EMCDDA, Report on the risk assessment of PMMA in the framework of the joint action on new synthetic drugs, Risk Assessments No. 5 (2003), ISBN 92-9168-137-7

freeodwiki.name: Cannabis
freeodwiki.note: FreeOD's oral-cannabis durations (onset 0.1–10, peak 15–45 min) are byte-identical to psychonautwiki's inhalation profile. A 0.1-min oral onset is impossible for cannabis; the data is mislabeled inhalation. Dose ladder (0.4–10 mg THC) is plausible for edibles and kept. Oral THC's psychotropic effects "set in with a delay of 30-90 minutes, reach their maximum after 2-3 hours" (Grotenhermen 2003, pmid:12648025).

tripsit.name: 4,4-DMAR
tripsit.note: common 60-120 mg. Glanville 2015 (Hum Psychopharmacol, pmid:25784180) records unwanted effects from 5 mg against desired effects at 10-200 mg — the ranges fully overlap — and 4,4-DMAR is linked to 31 European deaths in nine months. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

tripsit.name: Allobarbital
tripsit.note: light 500-1000 / common 1000-1500 / strong 1500-2000 mg for an intermediate-acting barbiturate. TripSit is the only source and no citable dose exists for the compound, so the ladder goes rather than being re-numbered.
tripsit.reason_only: No hypnotic dose and no per-tablet content for any allobarbital product is citable: openFDA has no label, and PubMed's 52 records use it as an HPLC internal standard, a mutagenicity test article and a rodent anticonvulsant. TripSit is the only source, its ladder runs in grams for an intermediate-acting barbiturate, and a replacement number would have to be invented, so the ladder is not shipped and none is written in its place.

tripsit.name: Changa
tripsit.note: Changa is a DMT-infused smoking blend; an oral route is a categorical error. Its ladder (5-50 mg) and timeline (onset 0-2 min, total 6-12 min) are the SMOKED values mis-assigned. DMT "is nearly inactive orally" without an MAOI because of rapid first-pass metabolism (Egger 2024, pmid:39254764).

tripsit.name: Midazolam
tripsit.note: total 4-8 h is a long-acting benzo's profile; midazolam's t1/2 is 1.5-2.5 h and it is chosen clinically FOR its ultra-short action. Intranasal midazolam's sedation set in within 5–10 min and lasted about 40 min (Gudmundsdottir 2001, pmid:11802661).

tripsit.name: Propoxyphene
tripsit.note: total 1-3 h against a measured single-dose half-life of 8-24 h for propoxyphene and 18-29 h for norpropoxyphene (Gram 1979, pmid:487695), both longer again on repeated dosing (3.3 to 11.8 h and 6.1 to 39.2 h, Inturrisi 1982, pmid:7056023) — a small fraction of the true duration, on a drug withdrawn for cardiotoxicity.

tripsit.name: Sufentanil
tripsit.note: total 5-10 min is the IV profile inherited verbatim. Swallowed sufentanil is 9% bioavailable and peaks much later than an injection: the half-time from Cmax is 2.5 h sublingually against 0.1 h intravenously (Willsie 2015, pmid:25544247). A user reading "10 minutes" on an ultra-potent opioid could fatally re-dose.

tripsit.name: Triazolam
tripsit.note: strong ceiling 1.5 mg is 3x the labeled MAXIMUM of 0.5 mg once daily (the recommended dose is 0.25 mg at bedtime). freeodwiki's 0.5-0.75 backfills and sits at the label ceiling.

tripsit.name: Furanylfentanyl
tripsit.note: light 200–400 / strong 800–1,600 µg insufflated and 300–1,600 µg oral on a compound with the highest MOR affinity of six fentanyl analogs, 3.8× fentanyl, mouse ED50 within ~1.3× of fentanyl (PMID 40721041); fatal femoral blood 0.41–2.47 ng/g (PMID 28096302). About 10× a lethal-range dose. TripSit's ladder verbatim.

tripsit.name: Acetaminophen
tripsit.note: common 200-500 mg ("Pain-relief 200-400mg | Fever 300-500mg") against the adult OTC label dose of two 325 mg or two 500 mg tablets, 650-1000 mg (DailyMed Tylenol Regular and Extra Strength). A 1000 mg dose, the commonly sold one, read as heavy. The curated label ladder replaces it.
tripsit.citation: DailyMed Tylenol Regular Strength and Extra Strength, §Directions

dosewiki.name: Acetylfentanyl
dosewiki.note: common 3-5 µg — about a tenth of fentanyl's own common dose, for an analog that sits within a decade of fentanyl in vivo rather than hundreds of times below it (pmid:40721041). The digits are the 3-5 mg ladder the other sources carry with the unit swapped. No source gives a defensible ladder (see the psychonautwiki, freeodwiki and tripsit entries), so this one is dropped too.

dosewiki.name: Furanylfentanyl
dosewiki.note: Same ladder as the TripSit entry (highest MOR affinity of six fentanyl analogs and a mouse ED50 within ~1.3x of fentanyl, pmid:40721041; fatal femoral blood 0.41-2.47 ng/g, pmid:28096302), on an expert-reviewed article; reported to dose.wiki 2026-09-11.

dosewiki.name: 5-MeO-DMT
dosewiki.note: dose.wiki's only oral entry: a 5-10 mg ladder with a 1-5 min onset and a 15-45 HOUR total. No orally absorbed drug acts within 1-5 min, and the total is an order of magnitude past any reported 5-MeO-DMT experience. The route is not claimed to be inactive — oral activity is reported, but only from 17 self-experiments (Ott 2001, pmid:11824699), against MAO-A inactivation as the compound's main clearance route (pmid:20942780) — so the whole route is dropped for want of a source that could carry a curve, not because the route does nothing. Reported to dose.wiki 2026-09-12.
